reviewed_by: Blind judgment Reviewer (subagent, 0 tool uses, samples inline), batch fix-loop-tick-2 2026-08-20

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The 'recognize' half is fulfilled squarely: seed 502 'Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend' (parallel), seed 600 'Two lines that cross at exactly one point' (intersecting), seed 44 'cross each other and form right angles / square corners' (perpendicular). The 'draw' half is never elicited: all 12 items are 4-option selections and no item asks the pupil to produce a construction. Seeds 43, 46 and 601 assess verbal knowledge ABOUT drawing; seed 45 is recognition wearing a drawing verb.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three relationships present but uneven: parallel primary in 5 items (42, 500, 502, 601, 604), perpendicular in 5 (43, 44, 45, 501, 602), intersecting in only 2 (46, 600). Intersecting is also the only relationship never anchored to a concrete object, while parallel gets the letter H and a ruler's edges and perpendicular gets the letter T and the model. By verb: recognize 8, draw-flavoured 4, actual construction 0.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Structure and single-step reasoning are right for Grade 3 Q1. Against that: authoring shorthand has leaked into pupil-facing text -- seed 44 reads 'form right angles / square corners ( ⟂ / + )' and seed 43 reads 'forming a square right angle', a redundant compound found in no textbook. The perpendicular symbol in seed 44 is formal notation not established anywhere else in the set. Seed 46's key phrase 'cross each other at a slanted angle' is not curriculum language.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five structures are present (blank completion, what-type identification, tool selection, procedure selection, yes/no relational), and seeds 602 and 604 are good items that probe family containment rather than labels. Against that: seeds 44 and 45 are functionally the same item (right angle -> perpendicular) with seed 501 a third pass at the same inference, and seeds 502 and 604 test one fact -- parallel lines never meet -- forward and then as a yes/no. Contextual referents are narrow: letters H and T and a ruler.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing reaches past scope: no degree measurement, no transversals, no lettered-point notation, no quadrilateral classification. Every keyed answer is one of the three named relationships or a procedure for producing one. Seeds 602 and 604 stay inside the competency by relating the three named terms to each other.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: No numeric magnitudes are involved. Four options per item, uniform; figures are single letters or a two-line crossing. Option strings in seeds 601 and 604 are at the top of the Grade 3 Q1 reading budget but remain single clauses.

problems_reported: Wrong keys, false statements, true-but-marked-wrong options: NONE FOUND. The reviewer checked the parallel/intersecting/perpendicular family in BOTH directions and confirmed soundness: every item keyed 'perpendicular lines' (44, 45, 501) omits 'intersecting lines'; seed 600, whose stem is equally true of perpendicular lines, correctly omits 'perpendicular lines'; seed 46 forecloses the overlap in the stem itself ('intersecting lines that are not perpendicular'), which legitimises its square-right-angle distractor. Seed 602 keys the containment explicitly and correctly.

All 12 seeds -- 'draw' is never performed. No item produces a construction. If the pipeline can emit a drawing/construction item type for this node, its absence is the gap; if it cannot, this set cannot evidence half the competency and that limit must be recorded rather than treated as covered.

seed 43 -- 'ruler only' is a semi-defensible distractor: a school ruler is a rectangle with square corners, so a pupil taught to trace a right angle from a corner could justify it. The keyed 'ruler and set square' is the curriculum method and clearly best, but the distractor is not cleanly false the way 'clock and ruler' is.

seed 44 -- 'line segments' distractor sits against a '+'-shaped model literally drawn as two segments; the stem's 'two lines that cross' plus the right-angle cue keeps the key uniquely best, but the option is softer than it looks.
seed 44 / 43 / 46 -- authoring shorthand in pupil-facing text: slash-alternates and 'square right angle' should resolve to one term before a pupil sees them.
seed 46 -- 'slanted angle' is technically wrong (the lines are slanted; the angle is simply not a right angle). Recommend 'cross each other but do not form a right angle'.
Coverage skew: intersecting under-represented at 2 primary items against 5 each, and never grounded in a concrete object.
seed 602 -- 'Only if they are rays' is incoherent as an answer to a yes/no about perpendicular lines intersecting; harmless to the key but dead weight.

Reviewer flagged 'ray'/'line segment' distractor vocabulary as undecidable from the packet. Resolved against ground truth after the review: both are in this node's cumulative_vocab, so there is no gating violation.
